assignment: CLI recon — locate where registration stored the shim; decide whether the official CLI is invoked AS `obsidian <subcommand>` (wrapper intercepts) or via a separate binary. Read-only; never execute /usr/bin/obsidian or `obsidian`.
answer: The CLI is invoked AS `obsidian <subcommand>` — but NOT via a wrapper that intercepts subcommands, and NOT via a separate CLI binary. It is the SAME Electron executable acting as a second-instance socket client. No shim exists on this host, and no `obsidian`-named CLI entry point exists at all, so `obsidian <subcommand>` currently resolves only to /usr/bin/obsidian (the GUI launcher).

mechanism.one_line: Second invocation of the same binary fails requestSingleInstanceLock(), connects to a unix socket owned by the already-running app, sends {argv,tty,cwd} as JSON, and prints the reply.
mechanism.impl_location: inside the Electron main process — /home/vgpnk/.config/obsidian/obsidian-1.14.4.asar (the app payload), NOT in /usr/bin/obsidian
mechanism.launcher_is_passthrough: true — /usr/bin/obsidian is a 344-byte bash script that only merges user-flags.conf then `exec electron43 /usr/lib/obsidian/app.asar $FLAGS "$@"`; it inspects no subcommand
mechanism.client_side: on lock failure: createConnection(socket) -> write(JSON.stringify({argv,tty,cwd})+"\n") -> zt(socket, vault, {executeCliRequest,...}) dispatches and prints
mechanism.server_side: the already-running main instance serves the socket; l.app.on('will-quit') -> unlinkSync(socket)
mechanism.enable_gate: if(!C.cli) return "Command line interface is not enabled. Please turn it on in Settings > General > Advanced." — C.cli is the flag persisted as "cli":true in obsidian.json
mechanism.critical_requirement: THE APP MUST ALREADY BE RUNNING. If no instance holds the lock, requestSingleInstanceLock() SUCCEEDS, the whole client block is skipped, and the process launches the GUI instead of answering.
